paper.title: Hybrid Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits with Probabilistically Triggered Arms

unmapped: Probabilistically triggered arms: semi-bandit feedback only on the randomly triggered set of base arms
Learner receives an offline dataset with N_i samples per base arm from a possibly biased distribution D^off
Learner knows a bias bound vector V with |mu_i^off - mu_i^on| <= V_i
Access to an (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle (not a linear optimization oracle); regret is (alpha,beta)-approximation regret
Reward function satisfies monotonicity and 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B
Reward is a general nonlinear function of the mean vector
settings.definition_quote: The online environment consists of $m$ base arms, represented as random variables $X_1, \ldots, X_m$, jointly distributed according to an unknown distribution $D^\text{on}$ ... supported on $[0,1]^m$ ... before online learning, the player is given an offline data collection $\mathcal{B}$ ... we adopt the bias control vector $V$ ... $|\mu_i^{\text{off}} - \mu_i^{\text{on}}| \leq V_i$

symbols.K_t: max number of arms that can be triggered by an action (paper's K)
symbols.Delta_min_i: minimum positive action gap among actions that can trigger base arm i
symbols.N_i: offline samples of base arm i

conditions: 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B (Condition 2)

source.label: thm:regret-bound
source.quote: For an H-CMAB-T problem ... that satisfies monotonicity (Condition~1) and TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~2), the hybrid CUCB algorithm with an input bias control vector $V$ and an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximation oracle achieves an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximate gap-dependent regret bounded by: ... where $N_i' = N_i \cdot \max\{ 1 - \frac{2BK \omega_i}{\Delta_{\min}^i}, 0 \}^2$.

results.notes: Regret is the (alpha,beta)-approximation regret defined via expected reward r_S(mu); recorded as pseudo_regret. Sum is over all base arms.

symbols.K_t: max number of triggerable arms per action (paper's K)
symbols.omega_max: max_i omega_i, omega_i = V_i + mu_i^off - mu_i^on
symbols.tau_star: optimal value of LP max tau s.t. tau <= N_i + n(i), sum_i n(i) <= K_t*T

conditions: 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B (Condition 2)

source.label: thm:gap-indep
source.quote: the hybrid CUCB algorithm with an input bias control vector $V$ and an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximation oracle achieves an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximate gap-independent regret bounded by: $\min\{ \psi, \gamma \} +4Bm + \frac{\pi^2}{6}\Delta_{\max}$ where $\psi = 8\sqrt{2}B \sqrt{\log (4mT^3)} ( \sum_{i} \max\{ \sqrt{KT/m} - \sqrt{N_i''}, 0 \} + \sqrt{mKT} )$, $\gamma = 16BKT\sqrt{2\log(4mT^3)/\tau_*}+BKT\omega_{\max}$

results.notes: The proof's final display for gamma reads 16BT sqrt(...) (without K); theorem statement with 16BKT recorded. Paper notes psi is between 8B sqrt(mKT log) and 16B sqrt(mKT log). Contains a Delta_max term despite being 'gap-independent'.
